summary: The bill amends Title 10 to require all appointments to the Military, Naval, and Air Force Academies to be made strictly in order of a standardized candidate composite score (with academics and test scores weighted at least 60% and 45% respectively and subjective factors capped at 10%), bars any consideration of race, sex, color, ethnicity, national origin, or religion, increases the number of ranked congressional alternates, adds 300 merit-based alternate slots per academy, and requires annual reports on minimum scores, waivers, and outcomes.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to government spending, budgets, appropriations, or fiscal outlays. It solely addresses admissions criteria and processes at the service academies.
The bill makes no changes to tax policy, rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare access, coverage, funding, or delivery systems.
The legislation does not mention firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No references to immigration policy, visas, borders, or pathways to citizenship.
The bill is silent on reproductive rights or abortion access.

While the bill reforms admissions to the military service academies (which train commissioned officers), it does not alter defense spending levels, force structure, procurement, or overall military budgets. The changes are procedural and merit-focused rather than fiscal.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related content appears in the bill.
The legislation does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net policies.

The bill mandates merit-based admissions emphasizing academics and standardized tests at federal military academies and bans consideration of race/sex/etc. This touches higher-education admissions policy but does not involve public K-12 schools, federal education funding formulas, school choice, or privatization mechanisms.
No provisions relate to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill contains nothing on sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization measures are present.
The bill does not address deficits, debt ceilings, or fiscal restraint measures.

The prohibition on considering sex (among other factors) in admissions could indirectly affect transgender applicants, but the bill's core purpose is race/sex-neutral merit selection rather than expanding or limiting LGBTQ legal protections.
No foreign aid, international assistance, or State Department funding provisions exist.
The legislation has no bearing on voting rights, election administration, or voter ID.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance content is included.
The bill does not address labor law, collective bargaining, or union rights.
The explicit ban on considering religion in admissions decisions enforces strict neutrality rather than creating religious exemptions or prioritizing civil-rights enforcement in other contexts.
